pr_title: Correctly support multiple events mapped to a single action
pr_body:
Currently, when multiple events are mapped to a single action, the state of the action is based on the last event that changed. This PR stores the state of each event to enable determining the correct state of the action regardless of which event last changed. This ensures that when two or more events are mapped to a single action, the Input `is_action_pressed()` reports true if any of the events are still pressed, and `get_action_strength()` returns the maximum value provided by all the events.

Properly fixes #30888 (reverts #30890).
Fixes #39287
Fixes #45628

~Note: I've tested this with keys and mouse buttons, but I've marked this as `needs testing`, because I don't have a joystick, so I can't test the `JoyButton` or `JoyAxis` events, specifically the combination of WASD keys and a joystick described in #39287 and #45628.~

**Edit:** I have now personally tested this with a controller to confirm that it does fix #39287 and #45628.
**Note:** It now includes automatically updating projects' input settings (i.e. it updates a project's `project.godot` file including the `config_version`). This means that projects opened with this PR cannot be opened with an earlier version of Godot (without restoring the `project.godot` file).
pr_comments:
Updated to fix issues identified by @mphe, and rebased to incorporate the changes made to `Input` since this PR was created. It now includes automatically updating projects' input settings (i.e. it updates a project's `project.godot` file including the `config_version`).

I have now personally tested this with a controller to confirm that it does fix #39287 and #45628.
At a quick glance, the concept looks good.  Does this handle Input.action_press() + Input.action_release() for code-triggered actions?

> Does this handle Input.action_press() + Input.action_release() for code-triggered actions?

This PR doesn't affect the behaviour of `Input.action_press()` or `Input.action_release()`.

> I seems that copy_action_values is kind of a workaround to store the values in the event we store in the input map, but IMO, this is very confusing.
> I feel that, if we need to store the action status, we need to augment the input map structure to store things alongside the event, not store things directly in the event itself.

What do you suggest as a better way to determine the status of each `Action`? I believe we need to keep a record of the last value associated with each `InputEvent` associated with each `Action`; so it's status can be determined when needed. Since, we're already storing the `InputEvent`s associated with each `Action` in the `input_map`. This PR simply uses this to also store each `InputEvent`'s last value.

The only thing I've added to the `InputEvent` API is the method `copy_action_values()` and separating the duplicate use of `axis_value` also being used for `axis_range`. Beyond that this PR actually simplifies the `InputEvent` API, by removing the secondary effect of `action_match()` sometimes also retrieving those same action values. This simplification will also allow a follow up PR to further simplify the API by merging `action_match()` and `is_match()`. I wouldn't call this _"modify the InputEvent API only for our needs in the action mapping system."_ never mind _"bloat the InputEvent API"_.

This PR is about properly supporting multiple `InputEvent`s mapped to a single `Action`. It's done using the data structures that are already there and hence _"keep the fix where it is needed."_. Whether or not the data structures should _"eventually"_ be changed is a separate question.

I am having the same issue — more than happy to provide test information etc, if needed to help resolve. I am on both Windows and MacOS, w/ Dualsense controller and keyboard set to same inputs (with goal to support seamless/automatic switching between different input devices for players). Let me know if I can be of help.
